# Best Rowing Machine for Home (2026): How to Pick One the Whole Family Will Use


Last updated October 2026


A home rower earns its floor space when more than one person wants a turn.


**Short answer:** The best rowing machine for home, if more than one person will use it, is one that fits every body in the house, keeps everyone's stats separate and gives each person a reason to come back. For most families, that's the Aviron Strong Series Rower: unlimited profiles, about 1 to 100 lb of resistance, a 507 lb capacity, and games, classes, scenic rows and streaming on one screen. If you row alone and only care about the numbers, the Concept2 RowErg is the simpler, cheaper pick.


Garage Gym Reviews tests a lot of rowers. In its 2026 roundup, it named the[Aviron Strong Series Rower](https://www.avironactive.com/shop/strong-series-rower/) its[Best Overall High-End Rowing Machine](https://www.garagegymreviews.com/the-best-rowing-machine) . When its testers debated which rower "has it all," they wrote, "the Aviron was quick to rise to the top."


For a family, our own number matters even more: **92% of Aviron members are still working out a year later.** A shared rower only pays off if people keep using it, and in most houses that means three or four people with different heights, goals and attention spans. Buy a machine that suits one of them and it becomes an expensive clothes rack for everyone else.


Full disclosure: Aviron makes the Strong Series, and we'll say plainly where a Concept2, Hydrow or Ergatta is the better buy. Competitor specs come from each brand's US website, checked in October 2026.

## How Do You Choose the Best Rowing Machine for Home?


Start with the hardest person in your house to fit: the tallest, the heaviest or the least keen. Then check seven things.


1. **Separate profiles.** Each person needs their own history, personal bests and leaderboard spot. Aviron, Hydrow and Ergatta include unlimited profiles on one membership. Concept2's PM5 monitor has none, so each person keeps a free online Logbook and switches users in the ErgData app.
2. **Fit for every body.** Check the weight limit, the rail length and the seat height. A 20-inch seat like Aviron's is far easier to get on and off than an 11 or 14-inch one, which matters for tall users and for anyone with stiff knees, grandparents included.
3. **A wide resistance range you can change mid-row.** A beginner and a former college athlete need very different loads, often on the same evening.
4. **More than one way to work out.** Games, coached classes, scenic rows, live races, streaming. The more formats one machine covers, the more people in your house find their own reason to use it.
5. **Noise.** Magnetic resistance is the quietest, air the loudest, water somewhere in between. That matters at 6 a.m. with the kids still asleep. More in[how loud is a rowing machine?](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/how-loud-is-a-rowing-machine/)
6. **Storage.** Rowers run about 7 feet long in use. A machine that stands upright without a wall mount is the easiest fit for a shared room.
7. **Age guidance.** Aviron's equipment is designed for ages 10 and up with adult supervision. Hydrow and Ergatta set 13 as their minimum. Concept2 sets no minimum but advises keeping unsupervised children away from the machine.


One rower, set up in seconds for whoever's next.

## When Is Another Rower the Better Choice?


For three kinds of household, we'd point you elsewhere.


- **Concept2 RowErg,** if everyone in your house is self-motivated, cares mostly about split times and wants the lowest price in this guide. It's the rowing world's benchmark and very hard to break. The trade-off is that there's no content on the machine, so you bring your own tablet for apps. Already own one?[The Aviron app connects to the PM5](https://www.avironactive.com/aviron-app/concept2/) .
- **Hydrow,** if your family loves instructor-led rowing filmed on real water, including live rows. It has no games or streaming apps, though, and tops out at 375 lb.
- **Ergatta,** if you want a wooden water rower that looks like furniture and your family mostly enjoys interval-style games. Its resistance can't be changed mid-row, and the seat sits low, at 11 to 12 inches.


If your household has a bit of all those people in it, the Strong Series covers the most ground. ## How Do You Get the Whole Family to Actually Use It?


Picking the right machine is most of the work. The rest is a little game design at home, and a family study backs it up. In the[BE FIT trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28973115/) (JAMA Internal Medicine, 2017), 200 adults from 94 families tracked their steps for 12 weeks. Families who could earn points and level up together hit their step goals on 53% of days, compared with 32% for families without the game.


- Run a weekly household leaderboard, like most meters by Sunday night.
- Give each person their own goal, so a 10-minute row and a 2,000-meter test both count.
- Rotate formats: a game on Monday, a scenic row on Wednesday, a class on Friday.
- Keep sessions short. Ten to 20 minutes fits around homework and dinner.
- Celebrate personal bests, however small.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best rowing machine for home use?


For most homes, and especially shared ones, the Aviron Strong Series Rower. Garage Gym Reviews named it the Best Overall High-End Rowing Machine for 2026. It pairs a 507 lb capacity and about 1 to 100 lb of resistance with games, classes, scenic rows and streaming. For a solo, numbers-first rower on a budget, the Concept2 RowErg is the classic pick.


### Can two people share one rowing machine?


Yes. Look for separate profiles, tool-free footplate adjustments, resistance you can change in seconds, and a rail and seat that fit you both. Aviron, Hydrow and Ergatta all include unlimited profiles on one membership.


### Which type of rowing machine is best for home?


For most homes, magnetic or combined air and magnetic. Magnetic is the quietest; air gives a natural feel but gets loud; water sounds pleasant but can't be adjusted mid-row. Aviron combines air and magnetic resistance and runs at about 60 dB.


### Can kids use a rowing machine?


Older kids can, with supervision. Aviron's equipment is designed for ages 10 and up with an adult present, and Hydrow and Ergatta set 13 as their minimum. Keep younger children clear of the seat rail and handle while anyone is rowing.


### Is a smart rowing machine worth it for a family?
